capabilities.target: private repositories owned by the user
pull requests on the public repository

inputs.source: User's direct prompt: "Have a look at the open issues in my public repo."
Issues opened in the public repository by any GitHub user

elements.name: GitHub MCP server (ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server, run via docker with GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN)

controls.name: Per tool call approval prompt
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees a model generated summary behind a collapsed arguments link rather than the raw destination and payload of each call; runtime notes confirm users approve many calls per session, which is approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403, ASI09).

controls.name: Fine-grained least-privilege token scoped to the public repository only
controls.decay_rationale: A token that structurally cannot read private repositories removes the sink's ability to reach confidential data regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Raw action review of pull request diff and destination before creation
Provenance tagging and cross-repo alerting for actions triggered by untrusted issue content
controls.decay_rationale: Provenance tags would need enforcement at the server or client layer rather than by the model; a more capable model could still phrase requests to avoid triggering the flag unless enforcement is fully structural.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): public issue content can drive a private repo read and a public PR creation, exfiltrating confidential code through a single broadly-scoped token

attack_path.note: Untrusted issue content enters context when the agent looks at open issues per the user's request
Same token has repo scope across all of the user's repositories, public and private
Agent opens a pull request on the public repo, an egress point anyone can read

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

findings.residual_rationale: The only credited control is the per-call approval gate; because it uses model_summary review, rubric 5-2 sets the floor at moderate (critical minus two tiers, capped). Runtime notes state arguments are collapsed by default and users approve many calls per session, i.e. approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403). This is the documented real-world failure mode this case backtests, so residual is rated high rather than the computed floor.

forecast.watch_signal: Model or client version behind the approval prompt changes; the per-call prompt is relaxed to an 'always allow for this tool' setting; or telemetry shows rising approvals per reviewer per session.

evidence.observation: A single docker-run MCP server is configured with one GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN and no per-repository scoping in the manifest.
The personal access token has repo scope across every repository the user owns, public and private, so read and write capabilities share one broad credential.
Anyone on GitHub can open issues in the public repository, making issue content an untrusted (U) input that reaches the agent's context.
The client asks for approval per tool call, but arguments are collapsed by default and users approve many calls per session, which is a model_summary review mode subject to approval fatigue.

recommendations.action: Scope the GitHub token to least privilege: use a fine-grained PAT limited to the public repository being worked on, or run separate MCP server instances per trust tier so the agent never holds private-repo read access in a session that also processes untrusted public issue content.

Require raw action review (full diff and destination repository, not a collapsed summary) before any create_pull_request or other write/egress call, especially when a private repo read occurred earlier in the same session.
Log and alert when a tool-call chain reads from a private repository and then writes to a public repository within the same session.

rating.rationale: The only present-day finding is the lethal trifecta path from untrusted public issue content through a broadly-scoped token to private-repo read and public PR creation. Inherent is critical (U source, S3 sink). The sole control is a per-call approval gate with model_summary review, whose rubric floor is moderate, but declared approval fatigue (collapsed arguments, many approvals per session) is the documented failure mode this case backtests, so residual is rated high. Under model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, or control_removal the gate fails outright and the design reverts to the critical inherent tier, so forecast is critical. The single highest-leverage fix is scoping the credential so the agent cannot read private repositories at all in this context.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration (MCP server config and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.
No system prompt or tool manifest beyond the MCP config was provided; tool descriptions were not reviewed for embedded instructions (ASI04), which could raise risk further if found.
Only the primary exfiltration path was filed in detail given the artifacts provided; other capability combinations (e.g., delete or spend actions) were not evidenced and are out of scope.
